name: Anantara New York Palace Budapest Hotel
positioning: Belle Epoque palace hotel on Erzsebet Korut Boulevard on the Pest side of Budapest, home of the New York Cafe
best_for: Travelers who want grand historic architecture in central Budapest
Guests who want a spa, indoor pool and gym included in their stay

facts.text: The hotel's architecture is an ode to Europe's Belle Epoque.
The hotel has a marble facade adorned with ornate carvings and a clock tower.
Inside, the hotel has columns, chandeliers and frescoes.
The building was designed by Hungarian architect Alajos Hauszmann.
The hotel is on Erzsebet Korut Boulevard on the Pest side of the Danube, near theatres, restaurants and bars.
The hotel is a short walk from the Madach Theatre, the Hungarian State Opera House and the Jewish quarter.
The hotel has an Anantara Spa, an indoor pool and a gym.
The 24-hour gym, the spa and the swimming pool are free for hotel guests.
Suites have separate living spaces, custom furnishings, chandeliers and oversized windows overlooking the city skyline.
Rooms have a marble bathroom with a bathtub.
The hotel is home to the New York Cafe, which has hosted the city's poets and artists for over a century.
The New York Cafe serves 24-carat-gold coffee and cakes.

highlights.text: The hotel has a vast Italian marble atrium with a glass pyramid roof.
Rooms in the original building open onto the atrium.
The newer block has more light, integrated tech and better outward views over the Budapest rooftops.
The hotel offers a guided city tour in a 59-year-old convertible VW Samba.
Hotel residents can skip the street queues at the New York Cafe and sit in the more intimate seating at the back.

considerations.text: The Great Boulevard the hotel sits on is very busy, though the noise does not seem to reach the rooms.
Rooms in the older section are showing signs of wear and need tech updates.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
